note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
Zion dwells with the daughter of Babylon. Who is the daughter of Babylon? “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof. O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed.” The children of Edom, E-D-O-M, meaning red people. So Edom is called the daughter of Babylon, and Judah dwells with Edom here in North America.

How do we deliver ourselves? “And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” That's how we deliver ourselves: by not being partakers in the sins of America, not taking part in their religious ceremonies, their denominations, their political groups and traditions. It's the same thing 2 Corinthians 6:17 says. “For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities. Reward her even as she rewarded you, and double unto her double according to her works.” Who is the you? The tribes of Israel. America is going to get double what they did to us, just as the psalm says: “happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.”

It may look like we've been forsaken, but “Israel hath not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, of the Lord of hosts; though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.” We are in a low state, destitute, degenerate as a people: the twerkers, the drug dealers, the homeless ones, that's how it's put out there. Regardless of all that, God has not forsaken us. “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel.” There is still hope for the pimps and the hoes, the prostitutes, the baby mama drama and the baby daddies.

“Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul: be not cut off in her iniquity; for this is the time of the Lord’s vengeance; he will render unto her a recompence.” The way you flee is to deliver your soul, and the way you deliver your soul is through repentance and keeping God's commandments.

precepts.why:
The Israelite way of life is structured so that if you lose your nationality, you are also cut off from your heritage. When they strip you of your identity, your laws, statutes and commandments follow it out the door; you stop performing the laws. Ezra prayed for “seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding”: culture is heritage.

So “If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.” The right hand is your strength; you usually work with your right hand. Jerusalem is our homeland, the place where you keep the laws and keep the feasts. Forget Jerusalem, and it is like forgetting your ability to work, the thing you know how to do.

Deuteronomy 33:2 shows what is in that right hand: “The Lord came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them; he shined forth from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of saints: from his right hand went a fiery law for them.” The law came from God's right hand.

So if you forget your identity, guess what else goes with it? Your way of life, the fiery law. Forgetting Jerusalem and losing the cunning of the right hand is losing the law along with the nationality.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
Who is the virgin daughter of Babylon? Let's identify her. “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” Destroy it, destroy it. Then, speaking to the same people: “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”. Edom is now called the daughter of Babylon, and she is destined to be destroyed.

So Isaiah 47 is the destruction of Babylon, which is Edom, the very thing David said in the psalm. “Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground”: you have been taken down, defeated. Then “there is no throne”: your throne is finished, your throne is over.

Then, “for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.” Babylon calls herself tender and delicate. How? The United States of America says, we are a Christian nation. She has two horns like a lamb, Republicans and Democrats, and says, we are Christian, in God we trust. That is the tender and delicate virgin, and God says she will be called that no more.

The children of Edom who cried to raze Jerusalem to its foundation are the daughter of Babylon today, America, and she is the one who is to be destroyed.

precepts.text: They that carried us away captive required of us a song.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
“For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.” “How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?” We read it right there in the history of the slave ships.

Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. What does Egypt represent? “I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.” Egypt is bondage. The Lord would bring us into bondage again, this time by way of ships; literal Egypt we would see no more again as a nation, and there we would be sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, slave men and slave women.

The Middle Passage, the Maafa, a massive disaster: for fifty days or more our people were packed in spaces as tight as coffins, a second platform barely twenty inches above the heads of those below, chained to the floor, lying in their own waste, amid rats that gnawed through wood and flesh, on floors covered with blood and excrement, where pregnant women gave birth and the living awoke chained to the dead. Tight packers crammed in as many as possible, reckoning the sales would offset the dead. The meal was horse beans pounded to a pulp with slabber sauce, once or twice a day, and a pint of water. Dumb negroes say it never happened and ask where the ships are: cargo ships carried spices and corn before us, carried us as cargo, and after slavery carried cargo again. Why get rid of them?

Then came the dancing of the slaves: the crew played the bagpipe or forced our ancestors to beat out a rhythm while they jumped about, ankles rubbed raw by the leg irons, to keep the human cargo in salable condition. That is Psalms 137:3: those who carried us away captive required of us mirth. At night the cries rose; an enslaved woman explained the howling came from having dreamt they were in their own country and waking in the hold of a slave ship. A strange land indeed.

Millions were carried from Africa to the West Indies, North and South America and Europe, from Luanda, from the Congo, from Loango, where the old maps mark the Jews; the buyers and sellers both knew they were selling outsiders, not the same people. Deuteronomy 28:68 and Psalms 137:3 were fulfilled on those ships.

precepts.why:
The Most High made the cities waste and brought the sanctuaries to desolation, and would not smell the savour of the sweet odours: He was not accepting the sacrifices, and He used the enemy to destroy the sanctuary. The Babylonians destroyed the temple, then the Greeks, then the Romans.

When Babylon came against Jerusalem, Esau stood on the side cheering it on. David records it: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” The children of Edom are Esau, and in the day of Jerusalem they urged the destruction on to the foundation.

Then the scattering among the heathen with a sword drawn out after them: not only the scattering, but death and anguish sent among the people in the lands of the captivity.

note.label: Psalm 79: The Heathen Have Defiled Thy Inheritance

The heathen came into the inheritance and laid Jerusalem on heaps, and our people sat in Babylon as a remnant in a strange land. Our forefather King Zedekiah was taken with his sons and daughters, and Daniel was born there. That is why Psalm 79 says “We are become a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.” The neighbours in this context are the enemies, the other nations, the heathen, the same ones verse one says came in and defiled the temple.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
David resolves, “I will sing unto the Lord as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.” Psalm 137 shows what became of that song in captivity: “By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion. We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof.”

“For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.” Our captors wanted the songs of Zion for their own entertainment. The answer was a question: “How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?”

That is the difference between the psalmist singing to the Most High while he has his being, and a captive people whose harps hang on the willows in a strange land.
